zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنا الإنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ وهْنًا عَلى وهْنٍ وفِصالُهُ في عامَيْنِ أنِ اشْكُرْ لِي ولِوالِدَيْكَ﴾ — it has come in the tafsīr: ”وَهْنًا عَلى وهْنٍ“ is "weakness upon weakness," i.e. her carrying him made her grow weak time after time. The position of ”أنْ“ is accusative by ”وَصَّيْنا“; the meaning is: "We enjoined upon the human being: give thanks to Me and to your parents," i.e. "We enjoined upon him thanks to Us and thanks to his parents."

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإنْ جاهَداكَ عَلى أنْ تُشْرِكَ بِي ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ فَلا تُطِعْهُما﴾ — it is related that Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ mentioned that this verse was revealed on his account. That was because he had become Muslim, and his mother swore that she would not eat food or drink any drink until he reverted to unbelief. She remained three days neither eating nor drinking, until they forced her mouth — i.e. opened it — with a stick, so that she ate and drank. And it is related that he said: "Even if she had seventy souls and they departed, I would not have turned back from Islam."
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَصاحِبْهُما في الدُّنْيا مَعْرُوفًا﴾ — one says ”صاحَبْتُهُ، مُصاحَبًا، ومُصاحَبَةً“ (I kept company with him). The meaning of ”اَلْمَعْرُوفُ“ is the deeds that are deemed good. ﴿واتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ مَن أنابَ إلَيَّ﴾ — i.e. follow the way of one who returns to Me.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿يا بُنَيَّ إنَّها إنْ تَكُ مِثْقالَ حَبَّةٍ مِن خَرْدَلٍ﴾ — and it is read ”مِثْقالُ حَبَّةٍ“ — the verse, up to His saying ﴿لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾, i.e. "Subtle in bringing it out, Aware of its place." And it is said [about] ”فِي صَخْرَةٍ“: i.e. in the rock that is beneath the earth. It is related that Luqmān's son asked Luqmān, saying: "What do you think of the grain that is in the maql of the sea — i.e. in the diving-depths of the sea — does Allah know it?!" One says ”مَقَلَ، يَمْقُلُ“ when one dives. So he informed him that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, knows the grain wherever it is, even in the most hidden places, because a grain in a rock is more hidden than [one in] water; then he informed him that wherever it is, He knows it through His subtlety, Mighty and Majestic is He, and His awareness. This is a likeness for the deeds of the servants: that Allah will bring forth their deeds on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ﴾ [al-Zalzala: 7] ﴿وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ﴾ [al-Zalzala: 8].
As for the nominative of ”مِثْقالُ“ together with the feminine of ”تَكُ“, it is because ”مِثْقالَ حَبَّةٍ مِن خَرْدَلٍ“ goes back to the sense of ”خَرْدَلَةٌ“ (a mustard seed), so it is equivalent to "if there be a grain of mustard seed." Whoever reads ”إنَّها إنْ تَكُ مِثْقالَ حَبَّةٍ“, with the accusative, it is in the sense of "The thing you asked me about, if it be the weight of a grain," and in the sense of "A person's deed, even if it is small, Allah will bring it forth." It is also permissible: ”إنَّها إنْ تَكْ — with tāʾ — مِثْقالَ حَبَّةٍ مِن خَرْدَلٍ“, in the sense of "the story (al-qiṣṣa) [is that…]," as you say ”إنَّها هِنْدٌ قائِمَةٌ“ (it is [the case that] Hind is standing). If you said ”إنَّها زَيْدٌ قائِمٌ“, it would be permissible, except that the grammarians prefer that [the masculine pronoun] with the masculine, while with the feminine they permit both feminine and masculine: they say ”إنَّهُ هِنْدٌ قائِمَةٌ“ and ”إنَّها أمَةُ اللَّهِ قائِمَةٌ“, permitting both aspects. As for ”إنَّها إنْ تَكُ مِثْقالَ حَبَّةٍ مِن خَرْدَلٍ“, for one who does not permit ”إنَّها زَيْدٌ قائِمٌ“ this is permissible, because its sense is feminine, by referring "what" [Translator's note: the source has «ما»; the reference is to the thing spoken of] to the grain of mustard seed.

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلا تُصَعِّرْ خَدَّكَ لِلنّاسِ﴾ — and it is read ”تُصاعِرْ“, and in Arabic ”وَلا تُصْعِرْ“ is permissible, but I do not know of anyone who read it; since it is not transmitted, it is not to be recited. Its meaning is: "Do not turn away from people out of arrogance." One says ”أصابَ البَعِيرَ صَعَرٌ وصَيَدٌ“ when the camel is struck by a disease from which it twists its neck; so of the arrogant one it is said ”فِيهِ صَعَرٌ“ and ”فِيهِ صَيَدٌ“. As for ”تُصَعِّرْ“, it is by way of intensification; ”تُصاعِرْ“ comes in the sense of ”تُفاعِلْ“, as though you were opposing them with your face; and the meaning of ”تُصْعِرْ“ is "make your cheek cling to ṣaʿar," because there is no disease in a human being worse than arrogance. The meaning in all three is this meaning, except that ”تُصَعِّرْ“ and ”تُصاعِرْ“ are more intensive than ”تُصْعِرْ“.
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَمْشِ في الأرْضِ مَرَحًا﴾ — i.e. do not walk swaggering and conceited.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿واغْضُضْ مِن صَوْتِكَ﴾ — the meaning of ”اُغْضُضْ“ is: lower. From this is ”غَضَضْتُ بَصَرِي“ (I lowered my gaze), and ”فُلانٌ يَغُضُّ بَصَرَهُ مِن فُلانٍ“, i.e. he disparages him. The meaning of ”أنْكَرَ الأصْواتِ“ is: the ugliest of voices; one says ”أتانا فُلانٌ بِوَجْهٍ مُنْكَرِ الخِلْقَةِ“ (so-and-so came to us with a face of munkar features), i.e. ugly.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ الحَكِيمِ﴾ — its meaning is: "These verses are those verses which you were promised in the Torah." It may also be in the sense of "These are the verses of the Book." The explanation of the like of this has also preceded in Sūrat al-Baqara.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَوْا أنَّ اللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكم ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ﴾ — the subjection of what is in the heavens is the sun, the moon and the stars; and the meaning of their being subjected to humankind is benefiting from them in bringing their crops to fruition, and being guided by the stars in their routes. The subjection of what is in the earth is the subjection of its seas, its rivers, its beasts and all its benefits. ”وَأسْبَغَ عَلَيْكم نِعْمَةً ظاهِرَةً وباطِنَةً“ — and it is read ”نِعَمَهُ“ (His blessings), in the plural. Whoever reads ”نِعْمَةً“, it is in the sense of what He gave them of His tawḥīd, Mighty and Majestic is He; and whoever reads ”نِعَمَهُ“, it is for all that He bestowed upon them.

zajjaj:22-22.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَقَدِ اسْتَمْسَكَ بِالعُرْوَةِ الوُثْقى﴾ — i.e. whoever submits has grasped the saying "There is no god but Allah," and it is the firmest handhold.

zajjaj:27-27.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ”وَلَوْ أنَّ ما في الأرْضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أقْلامٌ والبَحْرَ يَمُدُّهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ سَبْعَةُ أبْحُرٍ ما نَفِدَتْ كَلِماتُ اللَّهِ“ — and it is read ”والبَحْرُ“, in the nominative.
As for the accusative, it is a conjunction onto ”ما“, and the meaning is: "If what is in the earth…, and if the sea…." The nominative is good, in two ways: in the sense of "and the sea — this being its state"; and it may be conjoined to the position of ”أنَّ“ together with what follows it, because the meaning of ”لَوْ أنَّ ما في الأرْضِ“ is "if what is in the earth were to happen to be…," since ”لَوْ“ requires verbs; but when ”أنَّ“ comes with it, verbs are not mentioned with it, because nouns and verbs are [both] mentioned with it [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense appears to be that the clause introduced by «أنَّ» stands in for the verb that «لَوْ» requires].
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ما نَفِدَتْ كَلِماتُ اللَّهِ﴾ — its meaning is "would not be exhausted." It is related that the idolaters said of the Qur'an: "This is speech that will run out and will be cut off." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that His words and His wisdom do not run out.

zajjaj:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿ما خَلْقُكم ولا بَعْثُكم إلا كَنَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ﴾ — its interpretation is: "except as the creation of a single soul, and as the resurrection of a single soul," i.e. Allah's power to resurrect all creation and to create all creation is like His power to create a single soul and resurrect a single soul.

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ في النَّهارِ﴾ — its meaning is: He makes the night enter into the day, the night of summer into its day; ﴿وَيُولِجُ النَّهارَ في اللَّيْلِ﴾ — He makes the day of winter enter into its night.

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿هُدًى ورَحْمَةً لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ — the reading is with the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "Those are the verses of the Book, in the state of guidance and mercy."

zajjaj:31-31.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ الفُلْكَ تَجْرِي في البَحْرِ بِنِعْمَتِ اللَّهِ﴾ — and it is read ”بِنِعِماتِ اللَّهِ“; ”بِنِعْماتِ اللَّهِ“ is also permissible, and ”بِنِعَماتِ اللَّهِ“, with fatḥa on the ʿayn, is also permissible. So there are three aspects in it when it is pluralised. Most of the reading is ”بِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ“, in the singular. As for the kasra, it follows the way of one who pluralises ”كِسْرَةٌ“ as ”كِسِراتٌ“. And whoever puts sukūn — and it is the best of its aspects — follows one who pluralises it as ”كِسْراتٌ“, because ”كِسْراتٌ“ [Translator's note: so in the source; the context requires «كِسِراتٌ», with two kasras] is rare in the speech of the Arabs: among the basic word patterns, only those in which two kasras follow one another have come, such as ”إبِلٌ“ (camels) and ”إطِلٌ“ (flank), and that is all. And whoever reads ”بِنِعَماتِ اللَّهِ“, it is because the fatḥa is the lightest of the vowels. The poet said:
وَلَمّا رَأوْنا بادِيًا رُكَباتُنا ∗∗∗ عَلى مَوْطِنٍ لا نَخْلِطُ الجِدَّ بِالهَزْلِ
(And when they saw us with our knees showing, at a place where we do not mix earnest with jest.)
The more common is ”رُكَباتٌ“, and ”رُكْباتٌ“ is better because of the heaviness of the ḍamma; but it [the form with two ḍammas] is more common in speech than ”نِعِماتٌ“ and ”كِسِراتٌ“.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِكُلِّ صَبّارٍ شَكُورٍ﴾ — Qatāda related that the most beloved of servants to Allah is the one who, when given, is thankful, and when tried, is patient. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the one who takes heed and reflects on the creation of the heavens and the earth is the one who is very patient and very thankful.

zajjaj:32-32.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإذا غَشِيَهم مَوْجٌ كالظُّلَلِ﴾ — He said of the waves ”كالظُّلَلِ“ (like canopies) because the waves of the sea grow large until they become as though they were canopies.
His saying: ﴿خَتّارٍ كَفُورٍ﴾ — ”اَلْخَتْرُ“ is the foulest treachery.

zajjaj:33-33.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلا مَوْلُودٌ هو جازٍ عَنْ والِدِهِ شَيْئًا﴾ — ”جازٍ“ is in the muṣḥaf without yāʾ, and the original is ”جازِيٌ“. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl mentioned that the preferred choice in pause is ”جازٍ“, without yāʾ. The original is ”جازِيٌ“, with ḍamma and tanwīn; the ḍamma was heavy on the yāʾ, so it was dropped, and the yāʾ and the tanwīn were left vowelless, so the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. It ought to have been with yāʾ in pause, because the tanwīn has dropped; but the eloquent among the Arabs paused without yāʾ, to show that this yāʾ drops in connected speech. Yūnus claimed that some trustworthy Arabs pause with yāʾ; but the preferred choice is following the muṣḥaf and pausing without yāʾ.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلا يَغُرَّنَّكم بِاللَّهِ الغَرُورُ﴾ — ”اَلْغَرُورُ“ is Satan.

zajjaj:34-34.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السّاعَةِ ويُنَـزِّلُ الغَيْثَ ويَعْلَمُ ما في الأرْحامِ وما تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ ماذا تَكْسِبُ غَدًا وما تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ بِأيِّ أرْضٍ تَمُوتُ﴾ — it has come in the tafsīr that these five are the keys of the Unseen of which Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَعِنْدَهُ مَفاتِحُ الغَيْبِ لا يَعْلَمُها إلا هُوَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 59]. So whoever claims that he knows any of these has disbelieved in the Qur'an, because he has contradicted it.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنَ النّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الحَدِيثِ لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ — and it is read ”لِيَضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ“ (that he may go astray from the way of Allah). Most of what has come in the tafsīr is that ”لَهْوُ الحَدِيثِ“ (idle talk) here is singing, because it distracts from the remembrance of Allah; and it has been related from the Prophet ﷺ that he forbade the sale of a singing-girl. It has also been said in the interpretation of this verse that ”لَهْوُ الحَدِيثِ“ here is shirk. Whoever reads ”لِيُضِلَّ“, with ḍamma on the yāʾ, its meaning is: to lead others astray; and if he leads others astray, he himself has also gone astray. Whoever reads ”لِيَضِلَّ“, its meaning is: so that his affair ends in misguidance; it is as though, even if he is not able to lead [others] astray, his affair will end in his going astray.
His saying: ﴿وَيَتَّخِذَها هُزُوًا﴾ — i.e. he takes the verses of Allah in mockery; the verses were mentioned in His saying ﴿تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ الحَكِيمِ﴾ [Luqmān: 2]. It has also come in the tafsīr that His saying ﴿وَيَتَّخِذَها هُزُوًا﴾ means: he takes the way of Allah in mockery.
